resources.string: Accessibility service: On, but not running

EdgeVol is switched on in Settings but isn\'t running. This happens when the phone stops it, for example when you clear recent apps. If it doesn\'t come back by itself within a minute, switch EdgeVol off and on again in Accessibility settings.
Still not running after that? Switch it off and on once more.
If your phone has Autostart or battery restrictions, allow EdgeVol to start and run in the background.

Xiaomi, Redmi and POCO phones close EdgeVol when you clear recent apps. Do two things once: allow Autostart (button below: switch EdgeVol on), then open Recents, long-press the EdgeVol card and tap the lock. Already done? You can ignore this.

Ready. Look for a thin, faint bar on the edge of your screen (on the right, a little above the middle, until you move it). Tap it to show your phone\'s volume panel, or touch and hold it, then drag it to either side.

EdgeVol uses Android\'s Accessibility service only to keep its small volume handle on the screen edge, above other apps. It does not read, collect or send anything on your screen, and it has no internet access. The handle only asks your phone to show its volume panel.
Open your phone\'s own volume panel to check that it works.

On Android 13 and later, apps installed outside an app store can\'t use Accessibility until you allow restricted settings. If the EdgeVol switch is greyed out, follow these steps, then come back and tap Enable.
